items.t: What the page covers: the whole City of Surrey's secondary-plan system — 36 plan tiles spanning City Centre, the Whalley/Guildford corridor plans (Scott Road, South Westminster, Guildford Town Centre – 104 Avenue), the Clayton/Cloverdale NCP set, the Newton set, and the South Surrey / Grandview Heights set. The City organizes its approved secondary plans by community and describes them as providing neighbourhood-level detail on land use designations and density, road networks, amenities and servicing; plan types are the General Land Use Plan (GLUP), the Neighbourhood Concept Plan (NCP) and the Local Area Plan (LAP).
The City's own community list has seven communities: City Centre, Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, South Surrey and Whalley.
Board geography: the SnapStats community "Surrey" has 15 sub-areas; two further board communities also sit inside the municipal boundary — Cloverdale and S Surrey White Rock.
Board-name rule: the board sub-area for Surrey City Centre is Whalley; "Surrey City Centre" is not a board sub-area name.
Serpentine: Serpentine is a board sub-area (owner ruling, Nov 1, 2026), with dual filing — board = Cloverdale, live-feed ground = South Surrey.

Plan currency warning that frames this whole page: the Surrey 2050 OCP update has rescinded or superseded some older NCP designations — East Newton North was rescinded; East Newton South, the East Newton Business Park and West Cloverdale designations were superseded, with the OCP's designations now guiding land use. A plan tile does not by itself prove a plan's designations are still operative.

Transit: the City states City Centre is serviced by four SkyTrain stations; TransLink states the Surrey-Langley SkyTrain is a 16-kilometre Expo Line extension along Fraser Highway from King George Station to 203 Street in Langley City, with an anticipated in-service date of 2029.

items.t: Secondary suites: under Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, one secondary suite may be permitted per single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit, a suite is not permitted within a coach house or garden suite, and a suite's habitable floor area may not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling unit.

A plan tile and the current zone can point in opposite directions on the same lot. Surrey's July 8, 2024 SSMUH rezoning (R1–R7 replacing RF/RH/RQ) now does small-lot permitting that older NCP designations predate — the zoning is what can be built as-of-right today; the plan shows where the City wants growth.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Surrey
Streets, schools and getting around Surrey

items.t: Board-name positions carried: Surrey City Centre is not a board sub-area name — the land is the Whalley sub-area — while "City Centre" remains the City's own planning name for the downtown plan area, which is how the City Centre Plan tile legitimately uses it.

How Surrey's plan system is organized: the City organizes its approved secondary plans by community — South Surrey, Newton, Cloverdale, Whalley, Guildford/Fleetwood among them — and describes approved plans as developed through community consultation and endorsed by Council, providing neighbourhood-level detail on land use designations and density, road networks, amenities and servicing. A General Land Use Plan (GLUP) is the overall framework for an area; a Neighbourhood Concept Plan (NCP) is the detailed neighbourhood plan under it; a Local Area Plan (LAP) does the same guiding work outside the NCP process.

The plan stack a Surrey parcel can sit under: the Official Community Plan (as updated by the Surrey 2050 update), a GLUP where one exists (e.g., Grandview Heights, Clayton, South Port Kells), an NCP or LAP for the neighbourhood, the Zoning By-law No. 12000 as amended July 8, 2024 for SSMUH, and any Development Permit Areas — each layer checked separately for the parcel.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Surrey

items.t: OCP — current bylaw: Surrey 2050, Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026. Bylaw No. 18020 is the replaced predecessor. Zoning is under Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000. The City records that some older NCPs' land use designations have been superseded or rescinded through the Surrey 2050 OCP update — East Newton North was rescinded and East Newton South's, the East Newton Business Park's and West Cloverdale's designations superseded, with the OCP's designations now guiding land use while the NCPs continue to guide amenities and infrastructure implementation.

Short-term rentals: permitted, owner-only — an owner must host from their principal residence, tenants cannot run one, and a City business licence is required first. Licence figure conflict, carried openly: $358/yr (Zoning By-law No. 12000, Part 4 s. B.7(d) and Business License By-law No. 13680, s. 60.1) versus the City's 2024 corporate report proposing $350/yr + fees — carry $358 with $350 disclosed, and direct any buyer to the City licence page before quoting either figure.

For Grandview Heights lots, start from the GLUP, not the neighbourhood tile: the City's structure puts the Grandview Heights GLUP over the individual NCPs (Darts Hill, Morgan Heights, North Grandview Heights, Orchard Grove, Redwood Heights, Sunnyside Heights).

blocks.text: Good to know about Surrey

items.t: One plan appears twice on this page. The "Newton Town Centre Plan" tile and the "Newton – King George Blvd Plan" tile both describe the same event — a new Newton Town Centre plan approved/adopted by Council on July 13, 2020 — in near-identical words, so one plan appears twice under two names.

A tile can be behind the City's current position. South Westminster's tile describes the original NCP area only, while the City's March 10, 2025 position (Corporate Report R048) concluded the plan update for the area's industrial/employment portion and identified Waterfront District and Transit Village study areas at Scott Road Station — and on Scott Road generally, the operative document depends on the segment and the stage (2022 corridor endorsement vs the July 8, 2024 Imagine Scott Road Visioning Study for the 72 Avenue segment). Do not price a lot off its plan tile alone.

Surrey replaced its OCP in 2026 — and rezoned for SSMUH in 2024. Bylaw No. 21900 ("Surrey 2050") was adopted June 15, 2026, and the July 8, 2024 SSMUH rezoning put R1–R7 zones in place of RF/RH/RQ. Any Surrey guide still citing Bylaw No. 18020 as the current OCP, or quoting former RF-12 / RF-SD zone names as current, is out of date.

The plan stack, not the tile, is the diligence. A Surrey parcel can sit under the OCP, a GLUP, an NCP or LAP, the current zoning and Development Permit Areas at once — each layer checked separately, in that order. The page's typical user is exactly the person who needs that order: a lot owner testing future density under an NCP, a buyer pricing a parcel's plan designation before offering, and an investor following the Fraser Highway / Clayton Corridor and City Centre growth areas.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Surrey
Local rules that affect duplexes in Surrey

items.t: Plan and zoning (Surrey): OCP = Surrey 2050 OCP Bylaw 21900 (adopted Jun 15, 2026) — Bylaw 18020 is replaced and is never stated as current. Zoning Bylaw No. 12000. Darts Hill — the City records the Darts Hill NCP as approved by Council on May 10, 2021, the fifth master-planned neighbourhood in Grandview Heights, with its designations incorporated into the OCP. Servicing: Subdivision and Development Bylaw 8830 (1986) applies. Streamside setbacks sit in Part 7A of Zoning 12000 and vary by stream class — no single riparian figure is ever stated. Surrey has no Supreme Court registry.

Surrey adopted its provincial SSMUH zoning change on July 8, 2024, when Zoning 12000's residential zones R1 to R7 replaced the RF, RH and RQ zones — RF-12/RF-12C became R4 and RF-SD (the semi-detached form) became R6 — so the zoning now does the small-lot permitting that older NCP designations predate, and a plan tile and the current zone can point in different directions on the same lot. Duplexes are the baseline form where SSMUH applies.
